reach.rationale: The application code reaches for nothing newer than ES2021-era, years-stable web APIs. The only recency is the build toolchain: TypeScript 7 and Vite 8 are both current stable releases, but very young majors (7 and ~7.5 months old), so the app isn't entirely on long-in-the-tooth versions.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:1-6 — all build configuration (and any future tooling risk) confined to a 4-line config file
app/package.json:14-15 — toolchain newness lives entirely in two devDependencies
app/src/api.ts:1-4 — API base URL resolution wrapped in one module (window.__API_BASE_URL__ + import.meta.env), the only environment coupling
containment.rationale: There are no experimental APIs in the runtime code to contain; the two recent toolchain majors are isolated in package.json/vite.config.ts and could be downgraded (e.g. to vite 7 / @typescript/typescript6) without touching app source.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:4 — deliberately conservative target (chrome120) rather than chasing Vite 8's new default
app/tsconfig.json:3,13 — ES2022 target, noEmit CLI-only usage; avoids any reliance on TS 7's breaking compiler-API changes
app/server.mjs:1-4 — production server uses only stable node:http/fs/path/url core modules
justification.rationale: No experimental API is used at all; the only recent choices (TS 7, Vite 8) are the current stable releases bought for build speed and currency, not novelty, and every spec-level feature is implemented with mature platform primitives.

findings.issue: Vite 8.0.0 shipped with Rolldown 1.0.0-rc.9 as its internal bundler (per Vite changelog); ^8.3.5 is stable but the underlying bundler line is young, and plugin ecosystem compatibility is still settling.
findings.suggestion: Nothing to change — the app uses a stock config with no Rolldown-specific options — but pin/lockfile awareness and a quick check on minor Vite upgrades is worth it for the next year.

findings.issue: TypeScript 7.0 is only ~3 months old and removed the programmatic compiler API (tools must use @typescript/typescript6).
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is since the project uses tsc purely as a CLI type-checker (noEmit); just avoid introducing tooling that imports the TS compiler API without switching to the compatibility package.

summary: This app is aggressively boring in its API surface: the only runtime dependencies are the DOM, fetch and Node core, with zero experimental, preview or unstable markers anywhere. The single source of newness is the recently-stable toolchain (TypeScript 7, stable 2026-07-08; Vite 8/Rolldown, stable 2026-03-12), both of which are the correct current stable releases and are cleanly isolated in the build config. Risk of upstream breakage is very low.
